title.text: NAIA Manila Airport Arrival and Transfer Guide

title_en.text: NAIA Manila Airport Arrival and Transfer Guide

tagline.text: From terminal checks to baggage, connections and city transport

location.label: Location
location.text: Ninoy Aquino International Airport, Pasay and Parañaque, Metro Manila, Luzon

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round; follow flight, construction, weather and congestion updates

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Depends on the itinerary; confirm departure and connection margins with the airline

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: Personal arrival-day allowance ₱1,200–2,500 for transport, meals and contingency; flights and hotels excluded

children.text: Ninoy Aquino International Airport is a main gateway to Metro Manila. Flights sharing the MNL code may use separate terminals. Confirm the terminal, baggage arrangements and onward journey for each booking. This is practical arrival, connection and departure guidance, rather than a terminal sightseeing route.

Save the flight number, date and terminal together. The map pin indicates the Terminal 3 building, not a common entrance for every flight. Use separate pins for Terminals 1 and 2 and check the actual operating carrier, especially on codeshares.

Airline assignments changed in 2026 and improvement works continue. Older lists and doorway photographs are not current floor plans. Compare your booking with airline notices, then follow airport displays and staff. Gallery images show their capture dates; counters and barriers can move.

The airport spans Pasay and Parañaque. Airside, immigration and security areas are controlled spaces. Observe architecture or memorials only from permitted areas after handling your journey; do not cross the complex simply to collect photographs.

blocks.title: Find the terminal for your flight

children.text: Check both airport code and terminal. Rules such as one terminal for all foreign airlines can become outdated. Look up every flight and operating carrier, and specify the correct building when arranging transport.

Do not assume checked baggage automatically reaches your final destination. Ask about collection, customs and recheck. Some same-terminal international connections use a transfer desk before immigration; show staff your itinerary first. Keep baggage tags and the onward booking accessible.

Free terminal shuttles are available, but eligibility, stops and intervals vary. Carry a ticket or confirmed booking and ask for the current stop and wait. Do not cross traffic based on an old bay number or wait until the connection becomes impossible.

blocks.title: Authorized ground transport and dispatch slips

children.text: Use official booths and designated pickup points. Match an app booking to its plate, driver and destination. Retain any taxi dispatch slip and check the fare method and tolls before departure. A verbal offer outside the organized pickup process is insufficient.

Arrival, departure and transfer routes differ even within a large terminal. Ask about lifts and assistance before negotiating levels with heavy bags. Check whether dining and rest facilities are landside or airside, and locate an information desk for disruptions.

Terminal 1 has a distinctive high-ceilinged hall and outdoor memorial space. These are observations along a permitted passenger route, not a reason to obtain special access. Respect traffic, queues, photography restrictions and boarding deadlines.

These are process stages, not sightseeing times. Allow separately for immigration, baggage, customs and transport. Set hotel departure and airport arrival targets separately, checking all airline cutoffs. Online check-in does not remove every remaining step.
Follow staff guidance through arrival, baggage and customs.
Confirm the meeting point and use official or app-designated pickups.
Match the vehicle and destination, then allow for traffic.
Ask the airline about terminal, baggage and immigration requirements.
Check shuttle eligibility and the current stop before transferring.
Complete any recheck and screening, then reconfirm the gate.

Specify terminal and arrivals or departures level in a vehicle booking. A wrong building can mean another road journey. Use permitted drop-off areas and designated parking for longer waits; actual access depends on road layout and traffic.

Distinguish terminal shuttles, city buses and longer journeys to another airport. Verify the operator’s timetable, seats, baggage policy and stop. Do not rely on a flight arriving in time for a last bus; prepare an alternative.

A station name containing Airport or Ninoy Aquino does not establish a direct link to your check-in hall. Plan the final segment separately. Consider luggage and mobility needs, and distinguish another airport from another NAIA terminal by checking airport codes.

Flight schedules, weather and holiday traffic matter more than a touring season. Recent operator advice recommends arriving at least three hours before international and two before domestic flights. These are not guaranteed processing times; add road travel and any special needs.

For overnight arrivals, confirm transport, food and other services rather than assuming daytime conditions. Update accommodation and pickup plans after delays. Ask airline staff about a threatened connection, including terminal, separate tickets and baggage.

An illustrative personal arrival-day allowance is ₱600–1,200 for city transport, ₱300–600 for food and water, and ₱300–700 contingency: ₱1,200–2,500. This is an allocation, not an airport tariff. Flights, hotels, lounges and longer journeys are separate.

Separate a free terminal shuttle from paid city transport. Metered, destination-priced and app-booked vehicles use different fare methods. Ask the airline or official counter which ticketed fees apply rather than treating every airport or travel tax as one charge.

Choose a transit hotel by terminal access, not distance alone. Confirm transport, late arrival, early departure and baggage arrangements. A short connection may not accommodate immigration, luggage, hotel time and re-entry to the airport.

Plan meals after confirming your gate and deadlines. Landside and airside outlets serve different passenger flows. Check current hours and dietary needs, follow security rules and never leave bags unattended at a table.

Save bookings, flight numbers and accommodation details offline. Agree on terminal, level, exit and pickup area, not just an arrival message. Keep documents and baggage tags accessible while charging devices or moving with companions.

If eTravel registration applies to your trip, check eligibility and timing on the government site and save confirmation. Avoid paid lookalikes and unsolicited requests for passport images. Verify nationality- and visa-specific entry requirements with the authorities.

Do not treat immigration, screening or staff work areas as photo spots. An existing photograph does not grant permission. Respect barriers and request appropriate facilities when travelling with children or bulky luggage.

For a changed flight or wrong terminal, consult official staff before accepting an unsolicited ride. Keep control of documents. Retain booking and dispatch evidence if transport problems occur, and never improvise a walk along airport roads as a shortcut.

Makati, BGC and Manila Bay are separate onward destinations. Do not automatically add sightseeing to a short layover; account for entry, baggage, traffic and recheck. Resting after arrival can make the following day easier.

A journey to Clark or another airport is not an internal terminal transfer. Allow for flight delays, road travel and the next check-in, verifying the actual bus or vehicle stop. Nearby shops are useful only when legitimate access fits your terminal and schedule.
